newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco CEOs can be deposed in suit - Florida judge.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco CEOs can be deposed in suit - Florida judge.

text.p: A Florida judge said Friday he would rule that the chief executive officers of the country's major tobacco companies must give depositions in a class action suit brought against the industry on behalf of smokers in Florida.

Most of the big tobacco companies have named new chief executives since the case, known as Engle vs. R.J. Reynolds Tobacco RJR Nabisco, Philip Morris Cos Inc et al., was filed in 1994, meaning that executives currently running the companies might not have given depositions previously.
"I'm going to allow those depositions to be taken again, except (Loews Corp's ) Lorillard, which is the same person," Circuit Judge Alan Postman said at a pre-trial hearing Friday.
A trial date of Sept. 8, 1997, has been set for the suit, which seeks compensation for all Florida smokers suffering medical problems caused by cigarette smoking.
